## Another occurrence, 2026-10-19 ג€” different predicate, same shape

Full run on `f01a24a` (main, after the #180 fix landed): **1 of 79 red, 275.5s**, in `env/adapters/plannotator-inbox.selfcheck.ts`, case *"a server that never answers the tool call: the message says why"*.

Unlike the earlier reports, this one **did capture the failing predicate**, because it is an assertion on a message rather than on process release:

```
FAIL a server that never answers the tool call: the message says why ג€”
wf inbox: send_message: no answer to initialize within 300 ms from C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe
C:\Users\Shay\AppData\Local\Temp\wf-inbox-0LVCYp\fake-inbox.cjs (cwd ג€¦\wf-inbox-0LVCYp\wt); killed it
```

The fixture (`call-hang`) answers `initialize` and then stops: the check expects the message to name `tools/call`. Under the aggregate run the fake child had not answered its **own** `initialize` before that 300 ms deadline expired, so the adapter correctly reported the initialize timeout and the assertion on the wording failed. The behaviour was right; the expectation lost a race.

- Isolated, same tree: 3 consecutive runs of `node env/adapters/plannotator-inbox.selfcheck.ts`, exit 0, zero FAIL lines.
- Unchanged retry, full suite: **79 green in 247.7s**.

So this is the same family as the release refusals ג€” a short deadline in a selfcheck that holds only when its own child gets scheduled in time ג€” but it is a different module and a different predicate from the descendant-release path (`check-process.ts`/`process-tree.ts`). Recording it here rather than opening a second issue, since the fix likely belongs to the same class (a selfcheck that asserts on a 300 ms transport deadline while the suite runs its modules in parallel). It is not evidence that the inbox adapter leaked a process: the case's own "no process left behind" arm passed.
PR for the diagnostics step and the inbox fixture race: the release refusal now names its failed predicate. The cause is still open; waiting for the next occurrence.

## Diagnostic attempt, 2026-10-27 ג€” main `84b66d3`

**Keep open: no spontaneous descendant-release refusal captured, no cause established, no production change.**

Measured in a separate `diagnose/173-release` worktree:

| Execution | Observation |

The first baseline began on Node 26.10.0; subsequent attempts used 26.12.1. Final aggregate observed 26.12.1 before and after. A runtime replacement may have affected the initial ENOENT, but this is not proof of its cause or of the release failure's cause.

### Separate signatures in the final aggregate

- boundary: `bin/wfk.selfcheck.ts` imports `../env/shim.ts`; reproduced isolated.
- selfcheck fixture: missing `bin/wfk.mjs` in the copied inert tree, ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
- next / route: expected output no longer matches missing-ticket/Intent/no-measurement behavior; route then reads nonexistent checks.log.
- delivered-round / post-lifecycle: tracker-account-readback fixture mismatch (`/rest/api/2/myself`) and dependent assertions.
- serve: compound assertions on CI-wait preservation and copied PID refusal failed, but did not identify the failed subpredicate. CLI output showed refusal of the unverified PID with ownership retained. Not a captured native release refusal.
- content-identity / deliver-recovery / post-lifecycle: per-check 300s timeouts. Do not count these as release predicates.

### Evidence retained locally

`C:/Users/Shay/work/wf-173-evidence/` holds aggregate logs, focused/stress logs, per-module final output, external capture scripts and `aggregate-captured-final-report.md`. No pre-existing process was manually killed, no guard weakened, no production timeout changed, and no branch published.

The diagnostic gap is concrete: the normal suite buffers a failed check's output until every check finishes, and check-process's happy-status assertion omits its stderr. A runner crash can therefore lose the release predicate despite the existing production diagnostics. The external capture scripts close that gap for further reproduction attempts; they are diagnostic artifacts, not a proposed production fix.

Diagnostic evidence-loss fix merged in #231 (merge commit 683e648). Failures now print as each check finishes; native spawn errors become failed results rather than aggregate crashes; process happy-status failures include stderr. Focused checks and independent review passed. This is not a fix or a root-cause determination for the intermittent release refusal: keep #173 open. Diagnostic scripts, logs and reports remain at C:/Users/Shay/work/wf-173-evidence/. The clean diagnostic worktree has been removed.

# #173 native follow-up: fix lost deadline reason and retain release evidence

## Result

A confirmed timeout/cancellation reporting defect is fixed. The historical spontaneous descendant-release refusal is still not established as the same cause. Keep #173 open.

```text
Observed before
  runner exits 0 -> finish begins native cleanup
  deadline fires -> cancelled=true -> second finish call returns at finishing guard
  cleanup confirms release -> status=null, stderr=""

After
  cancellation records its reason before calling finish
  finishing guard still prevents duplicate cleanup
  result remains status=null and reports timed out/cancelled
```

The timeout budget, status invalidation, native identity checks and release predicates stay in place.

## Additional diagnostic gaps fixed

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Native kill returns only false | Optional bounded failure evidence identifies the native stage, PID and native error code; boolean callers remain compatible |
| Orphan-state write drops the release diagnosis | The retained record includes the diagnosis, orphan count and at most ten observed orphan identities |
| Runner-start error is discarded | Native error code and exit signal are filtered before rendering; no full error message or command is retained |

Orphan identities remain evidence only. They are not added to the authorized kill set. Unknown inventory remains a refusal.

## Reproduction and proof

| Command or witness | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Controlled native identity mismatch | false with no failure evidence; regression red | false with identity-mismatch; mismatched process stays alive |
| Abort during native cleanup through a wrapper around the real kill operation | null status with empty stderr; regression red | null status with cancelled; regression green |
| Native orphan fixture | orphan refusal record lacks diagnosis; removing retention makes the new regression red | refusal and observed orphan identity retained |
| Four concurrent workers, eight immediate-exit runs each | 30 zero exits, two unexplained null results | 32/32 zero exits; no null results or release refusals |
| Three native runs with a 1500ms deadline | Debug trace captured the deadline while finishing; two had empty reasons | Three explicit timeouts; all remain nonmeasurements, not green proof |

Key trace in `native-missing-status-debug.log`:

```text
finish: status=0, reason='', finishing=false
late timer: reason='timed out', finishing=true
resolve: released=true, cancelled=true, status=0
returned: status=null, stderr=''
```

The native kill diagnostic callback also has real missing-executable coverage. Runner-start errors have real ENOENT coverage. Self-PID and mismatched creation identities remain protected.

## Focused verification

- Native/process/browser checks plus tsc and ESLint: **7 green**, 58.3s.
- Server interruption/recovery/startup/verification plus tsc and ESLint: **6 green**, 44.4s.
- Final process-tree/check-process/check-orphan plus tsc and ESLint after test cleanup correction: **5 green**, 41.7s.
- Independent reviewer ran native checks plus tsc/ESLint: **5 green** and found no production blockers.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

These are focused results. No new complete aggregate result is claimed. The nine previously recorded baseline aggregate failures are not represented as fixed by this patch.

## Scope and files

```text
~ src/process-tree.ts                    bounded kill-failure callback; handle/creation-time guard retained
~ src/gates/check-process.ts             preserve late cancellation reason and refusal diagnostics
~ src/gates/check-supervisor.ts          report native runner-start code and exit signal
~ src/process-tree.selfcheck.ts          native mismatch/self/absent-probe witnesses and recovery-safe fixture
~ src/gates/check-process.selfcheck.ts   ENOENT, retained failure metadata and late-cancel regression
+ src/gates/check-orphan.selfcheck.ts    real orphan refusal and retained diagnosis
```
